title: The Hundredth Piece
logline: Before the New Year, a sweet-maker's hands move without looking, and a child's whole day depends on the first bite.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a feast's second and third helpings to a kitchen before the New Year, where the maker's hands no longer need to look and a child's day hangs on the first bite.

thread_out.thread: The same New Year season, far to the north: after the sweets, the new clothes, and the different reasons people give for wanting them.

requirements: A family actively making traditional sweets for the New Year
Consent to film children in a home setting, from parents or guardians
A kitchen with room for close, unobtrusive filming

lesson.in_simple_terms: Every taste arrives with a feeling already in it: pleasant, unpleasant, or neither. In one kitchen, the same sweet can bring a child pure delight and bring the hands that made it almost nothing at all.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: සෑම රසයකටම ප්‍රිය, අප්‍රිය හෝ මැදහත් වේදනාවක් එක්ව එන අතර, එකම කැවිල්ල දරුවෙකුට මහත් සතුටක් වුවත් එය සෑදූ අයට සාමාන්‍ය දෙයක් විය හැකිය.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma calls feeling (vedanā) the 'tasting' of an object's flavour and says it is present in every mind, because every mind takes an object; as objects vary, feeling varies with them. It is experienced in only three ways, pleasant, painful or neutral. The texts count joy (somanassa) in many kinds of mind, including wanting minds but also kind, generous and deeply concentrated ones, and count neutral feeling (upekkhā) in many others, so neither tone is good or bad in itself.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The camera stays with the maker's hands, moving without looking after hundreds of pieces, and then with children waiting for the first batch to cool. Cutting between the maker's flat rhythm, an elder's careful tasting and a child's first bite lets the viewer notice three different feelings meeting the same sweet, without anyone saying so.

key_terms.en: feeling: the tasting of an object's flavour

lesson.caution: This does not mean that pleasure is the enemy, or that the texts say wanting always starts from pleasure: they find pleasant feeling in many kind and wholesome moments, and wanting can come with flat feeling too.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed wanting arriving pleasant or flat at a crowded table; this one slows down on the feeling itself, the taste that comes with every experience and differs from one person to the next over the same sweet.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
